title: Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2019 (EESM19)
description: The Ear-EEG Sleep Monitoring 2019 (EESM19) dataset comprises polysomnographic and ear-EEG recordings collected from 20 subjects over multiple nights in home settings between 2018 and 2020. The dataset includes concurrent measurements from partial PSG (EEG, EOG, chin EMG), ear-EEG electrodes, wrist-worn actigraphy, and subjective sleep quality assessments. This resource supports the development and validation of ear-EEG as a practical sleep monitoring platform.
methods_description: Data collection involved 20 subjects sleeping in their own homes. Part A consisted of 4 nights per subject with simultaneous partial PSG (EEG, EOG, chin EMG electrodes), ear-EEG, and wrist-worn GENEactive actigraph recordings. Part B included 10 of these subjects completing an additional 12 nights wearing only ear-EEG, actigraph, and a single EOG electrode. Each night was recorded as a separate session. Electrode quality was assessed using a standardized electrode test protocol involving jaw clenching, eye opening/closing, and horizontal eye movements. Post-collection, faulty electrodes with signal leakage were identified and marked as NaN in the processed data.
